04 / ENGINEERING DECISIONS

Technology choices need context.

I evaluate options by workload, team maturity, failure modes, operational cost and the ability to evolve—not by trend.

01Modular Monolith vs Microservices+

Start with boundaries, not deployment units. Microservices earn their place when independent scaling, ownership or release cadence creates measurable value.

BOUNDARIES · OWNERSHIP · OPERATIONAL COST
02Virtual Threads vs Reactive+

Virtual threads simplify high-concurrency blocking workloads. Reactive remains valuable where end-to-end streaming and backpressure are core requirements.

CONCURRENCY · COMPLEXITY · BACKPRESSURE
03Kafka vs Traditional Queues+

Kafka fits replay, high event volume and ordered processing by key. Traditional brokers often reduce complexity for command-style queues and routing-heavy flows.

REPLAY · ORDERING · DELIVERY SEMANTICS
04SQL vs NoSQL+

Choose from access patterns and consistency needs. Relational databases remain a strong default; specialized NoSQL models solve specific scale and shape constraints.

CONSISTENCY · ACCESS PATTERNS · DATA SHAPE
